13 /-!
14 # Sets
15 
16 This file sets up the theory of sets whose elements have a given type.
17 
18 ## Main definitions
19 
20 Given a type `X` and a predicate `p : X → Prop`:
21 
22 * `Set X` : the type of sets whose elements have type `X`
23 * `{a : X | p a} : Set X` : the set of all elements of `X` satisfying `p`
24 * `{a | p a} : Set X` : a more concise notation for `{a : X | p a}`
25 * `{f x y | (x : X) (y : Y)} : Set Z` : a more concise notation for `{z : Z | ∃ x y, f x y = z}`
26 * `{a ∈ S | p a} : Set X` : given `S : Set X`, the subset of `S` consisting of
27   its elements satisfying `p`.
28 
29 ## Implementation issues
30 
31 As in Lean 3, `Set X := X → Prop`
32 This file is a port of the core Lean 3 file `lib/lean/library/init/data/set.lean`.
33 
34 -/
35 
36 @[expose] public section
37 
38 open Lean Elab Term Meta Batteries.ExtendedBinder
39 
40 universe u
41 variable {α : Type u}
42 
43 /-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.
44 
45 Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
46 relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
47 and predicates.
48 -/
49 def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop
50 
51 /-
52 We don't translate the order on sets (i.e. turning `s ⊆ t` into `t ⊆ s`).
53 This is because for example the following theorems should be dual
54 ```
55 theorem sSup_le_sSup {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : sSup s ≤ sSup t
56 theorem sInf_le_sInf {s t : Set α} (h : s ⊆ t) : sInf t ≤ sInf s
57 ```
58 Additionally, dualizing the order on sets would mean that a set is dual to its complement.
59 But we would like to dualize set intervals such that e.g. `Ico a b` is dual to `Ioc b a`.
60 -/
61 attribute [to_dual_dont_translate] Set
62 
63 /-- Turn a predicate `p : α → Prop` into a set, also written as `{x | p x}` -/
64 def setOf {α : Type u} (p : α → Prop) : Set α :=
65   p
66 
67 namespace Set
68 
69 /-- Membership in a set -/
70 protected def Mem (s : Set α) (a : α) : Prop :=
71   s a
72 
73 instance : Membership α (Set α) :=
74   ⟨Set.Mem⟩
75 
76 @[ext, grind ext]
77 theorem ext {a b : Set α} (h : ∀ (x : α), x ∈ a ↔ x ∈ b) : a = b :=
78   funext (fun x ↦ propext (h x))
79 
80 /-- The subset relation on sets. `s ⊆ t` means that all elements of `s` are elements of `t`.
81 
82 Note that you should **not** use this definition directly, but instead write `s ⊆ t`. -/
83 protected def Subset (s₁ s₂ : Set α) :=
84   ∀ ⦃a⦄, a ∈ s₁ → a ∈ s₂
85 
86 /-- We introduce `≤` before `⊆` to help the unifier when applying lattice theorems
87 to subset hypotheses. -/
88 instance : LE (Set α) :=
89   ⟨Set.Subset⟩
90 
91 instance : HasSubset (Set α) :=
92   ⟨(· ≤ ·)⟩
93 
94 instance : EmptyCollection (Set α) :=
95   ⟨fun _ ↦ False⟩
96 
97 end Set

99 namespace Mathlib.Meta
100 
101 /-- Set builder syntax. This can be elaborated to either a `Set` or a `Finset` depending on context.
102 
103 The elaborators for this syntax are located in:
104 * `Data.Set.Defs` for the `Set` builder notation elaborator for syntax of the form `{x | p x}`,
105   `{x : α | p x}`, `{binder x | p x}`.
106 * `Data.Finset.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator for syntax of the form
107   `{x ∈ s | p x}`.
108 * `Data.Fintype.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator for syntax of the form
109   `{x | p x}`, `{x : α | p x}`, `{x ∉ s | p x}`, `{x ≠ a | p x}`.
110 * `Order.LocallyFinite.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator for syntax of the form
111   `{x ≤ a | p x}`, `{x ≥ a | p x}`, `{x < a | p x}`, `{x > a | p x}`.
112 -/
113 syntax (name := setBuilder) "{" extBinder " | " term "}" : term
114 
115 /-- Elaborate set builder notation for `Set`.
116 
117 * `{x | p x}` is elaborated as `Set.setOf fun x ↦ p x`
118 * `{x : α | p x}` is elaborated as `Set.setOf fun x : α ↦ p x`
119 * `{binder x | p x}`, where `x` is bound by the `binder` binder, is elaborated as
120   `{x | binder x ∧ p x}`. The typical example is `{x ∈ s | p x}`, which is elaborated as
121   `{x | x ∈ s ∧ p x}`. The possible binders are
122   * `· ∈ s`, `· ∉ s`
123   * `· ⊆ s`, `· ⊂ s`, `· ⊇ s`, `· ⊃ s`
124   * `· ≤ a`, `· ≥ a`, `· < a`, `· > a`, `· ≠ a`
125 
126   More binders can be declared using the `binder_predicate` command, see `Init.BinderPredicates` for
127   more info.
128 
129 See also
130 * `Data.Finset.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator partly overriding this one for
131   syntax of the form `{x ∈ s | p x}`.
132 * `Data.Fintype.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator partly overriding this one for
133   syntax of the form `{x | p x}`, `{x : α | p x}`, `{x ∉ s | p x}`, `{x ≠ a | p x}`.
134 * `Order.LocallyFinite.Basic` for the `Finset` builder notation elaborator partly overriding this
135   one for syntax of the form `{x ≤ a | p x}`, `{x ≥ a | p x}`, `{x < a | p x}`, `{x > a | p x}`.
136 -/
137 @[term_elab setBuilder]
138 meta def elabSetBuilder : TermElab
139   | `({ $x:ident | $p }), expectedType? => do
140     elabTerm (← `(setOf fun $x:ident ↦ $p)) expectedType?
141   | `({ $x:ident : $t | $p }), expectedType? => do
142     elabTerm (← `(setOf fun $x:ident : $t ↦ $p)) expectedType?
143   | `({ $x:ident $b:binderPred | $p }), expectedType? => do
144     elabTerm (← `(setOf fun $x:ident ↦ satisfies_binder_pred% $x $b ∧ $p)) expectedType?
145   | _, _ => throwUnsupportedSyntax
146 
147 /-- Unexpander for set builder notation. -/
148 @[app_unexpander setOf]
149 meta def setOf.unexpander : Lean.PrettyPrinter.Unexpander
150   | `($_ fun $x:ident ↦ $p) => `({ $x:ident | $p })
151   | `($_ fun ($x:ident : $ty:term) ↦ $p) => `({ $x:ident : $ty:term | $p })
152   | _ => throw ()
153 
154 open Batteries.ExtendedBinder in
155 /--
156 `{ f x y | (x : X) (y : Y) }` is notation for the set of elements `f x y` constructed from the
157 binders `x` and `y`, equivalent to `{z : Z | ∃ x y, f x y = z}`.
158 
159 If `f x y` is a single identifier, it must be parenthesized to avoid ambiguity with `{x | p x}`;
160 for instance, `{(x) | (x : Nat) (y : Nat) (_hxy : x = y^2)}`.
161 -/
162 macro (priority := low) "{" t:term " | " bs:extBinders "}" : term =>
163   `({x | ∃ᵉ $bs:extBinders, $t = x})
164 
165 /--
166 * `{ pat : X | p }` is notation for pattern matching in set-builder notation,
167   where `pat` is a pattern that is matched by all objects of type `X`
168   and `p` is a proposition that can refer to variables in the pattern.
169   It is the set of all objects of type `X` which, when matched with the pattern `pat`,
170   make `p` come out true.
171 * `{ pat | p }` is the same, but in the case when the type `X` can be inferred.
172 
173 For example, `{ (m, n) : ℕ × ℕ | m * n = 12 }` denotes the set of all ordered pairs of
174 natural numbers whose product is 12.
175 
176 Note that if the type ascription is left out and `p` can be interpreted as an extended binder,
177 then the extended binder interpretation will be used.  For example, `{ n + 1 | n < 3 }` will
178 be interpreted as `{ x : Nat | ∃ n < 3, n + 1 = x }` rather than using pattern matching.
179 -/
180 macro (name := macroPattSetBuilder) (priority := low - 1)
181   "{" pat:term " : " t:term " | " p:term "}" : term =>
182   `({ x : $t | match x with | $pat => $p })
183 
184 @[inherit_doc macroPattSetBuilder]
185 macro (priority := low - 1) "{" pat:term " | " p:term "}" : term =>
186   `({ x | match x with | $pat => $p })
187 
188 /-- Pretty printing for set-builder notation with pattern matching. -/
189 @[app_unexpander setOf]
190 meta def setOfPatternMatchUnexpander : Lean.PrettyPrinter.Unexpander
191   | `($_ fun $x:ident ↦ match $y:ident with | $pat => $p) =>
192       if x == y then
193         `({ $pat:term | $p:term })
194       else
195         throw ()
196   | `($_ fun ($x:ident : $ty:term) ↦ match $y:ident with | $pat => $p) =>
197       if x == y then
198         `({ $pat:term : $ty:term | $p:term })
199       else
200         throw ()
201   | _ => throw ()
202 
203 end Mathlib.Meta
204 
205 namespace Set
206 
207 /-- The universal set on a type `α` is the set containing all elements of `α`.
208 
209 This is conceptually the "same as" `α` (in set theory, it is actually the same), but type theory
210 makes the distinction that `α` is a type while `Set.univ` is a term of type `Set α`. `Set.univ` can
211 itself be coerced to a type `↥Set.univ` which is in bijection with (but distinct from) `α`. -/
212 def univ : Set α := {_a | True}
213 
214 /-- `Set.insert a s` is the set `{a} ∪ s`.
215 
216 Note that you should **not** use this definition directly, but instead write `insert a s` (which is
217 mediated by the `Insert` typeclass). -/
218 protected def insert (a : α) (s : Set α) : Set α := {b | b = a ∨ b ∈ s}
219 
220 instance : Insert α (Set α) := ⟨Set.insert⟩
221 
222 /-- The singleton of an element `a` is the set with `a` as a single element.
223 
224 Note that you should **not** use this definition directly, but instead write `{a}`. -/
225 protected def singleton (a : α) : Set α := {b | b = a}
226 
227 instance instSingletonSet : Singleton α (Set α) := ⟨Set.singleton⟩
228 
229 /-- The union of two sets `s` and `t` is the set of elements contained in either `s` or `t`.
230 
231 Note that you should **not** use this definition directly, but instead write `s ∪ t`. -/
232 protected def union (s₁ s₂ : Set α) : Set α := {a | a ∈ s₁ ∨ a ∈ s₂}
233 
234 instance : Union (Set α) := ⟨Set.union⟩
235 
236 /-- The intersection of two sets `s` and `t` is the set of elements contained in both `s` and `t`.
237 
238 Note that you should **not** use this definition directly, but instead write `s ∩ t`. -/
239 protected def inter (s₁ s₂ : Set α) : Set α := {a | a ∈ s₁ ∧ a ∈ s₂}
240 
241 instance : Inter (Set α) := ⟨Set.inter⟩
242 
243 /-- The complement of a set `s` is the set of elements not contained in `s`.
244 
245 Note that you should **not** use this definition directly, but instead write `sᶜ`. -/
246 protected def compl (s : Set α) : Set α := {a | a ∉ s}
247 
248 /-- The difference of two sets `s` and `t` is the set of elements contained in `s` but not in `t`.
249 
250 Note that you should **not** use this definition directly, but instead write `s \ t`. -/
251 protected def diff (s t : Set α) : Set α := {a ∈ s | a ∉ t}
252 
253 instance : SDiff (Set α) := ⟨Set.diff⟩
254 
255 /-- `𝒫 s` is the set of all subsets of `s`. -/
256 def powerset (s : Set α) : Set (Set α) := {t | t ⊆ s}
257 
258 @[inherit_doc] prefix:100 "𝒫 " => powerset
259 
260 universe v in
261 /-- The image of `s : Set α` by `f : α → β`, written `f '' s`, is the set of `b : β` such that
262 `f a = b` for some `a ∈ s`. -/
263 def image {β : Type v} (f : α → β) (s : Set α) : Set β := {f a | a ∈ s}
264 
265 instance : Functor Set where map := @Set.image
266 
267 instance : LawfulFunctor Set where
268   id_map _ := funext fun _ ↦ propext ⟨fun ⟨_, sb, rfl⟩ ↦ sb, fun sb ↦ ⟨_, sb, rfl⟩⟩
269   comp_map g h _ := funext <| fun c ↦ propext
270     ⟨fun ⟨a, ⟨h₁, h₂⟩⟩ ↦ ⟨g a, ⟨⟨a, ⟨h₁, rfl⟩⟩, h₂⟩⟩,
271      fun ⟨_, ⟨⟨a, ⟨h₁, h₂⟩⟩, h₃⟩⟩ ↦ ⟨a, ⟨h₁, show h (g a) = c from h₂ ▸ h₃⟩⟩⟩
272   map_const := rfl
273 
274 /-- The property `s.Nonempty` expresses the fact that the set `s` is not empty. It should be used
275 in theorem assumptions instead of `∃ x, x ∈ s` or `s ≠ ∅` as it gives access to a nice API thanks
276 to the dot notation. -/
277 protected def Nonempty (s : Set α) : Prop :=
278   ∃ x, x ∈ s
279 
280 end Set
